newsitem.title: CANADA: Golden Rule sinks on Ghana drill results.
newsitem.headline: Golden Rule sinks on Ghana drill results.

text.p: Shares in Golden Rule Resources Ltd sank more than 50 percent on Wednesday after the company said earlier promising assays for its gold property in Ghana were unreliable.
Golden Rule stock was off 1.12 at 1.08 in brisk midday turnover of 1.5 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
"The earlier wonderful results they got from Ghana are not that wonderful anymore. That's the reason for the selloff," one Canadian mining analyst said.
The stock hit a 52-week low of 0.85 when it resumed trading today. It was halted for the release of new test results on Tuesday.
"The inability to reproduce the initial high gold-in-soil assay results indicates that the original data is unreliable," Golden Rule said in a statement on Tuesday.
The company said it planned to conduct further tests using a new sampling protocol.
Golden Rule's stock soared to a high of 13.10 in January after the company reported high gold assay values from the Stenpad property.

But investors dumped the stock in May when two independent tests suggested Golden Rule's findings had been overstated. Golden Rule subsequently hired Associated Mining Consultants Ltd to review its exploration of the property.
Associated Mining's report would be available sometime in the next week, Golden Rule said.
The Stenpad project is owned 50 percent each by Golden Rule and Hixon Gold Resources Inc.
